an4.41:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these four ways of developing concentration further.
an4.41:1.3: There is a way of developing concentration further that leads to pleasant abiding here and now.
an4.41:1.4: There is a way of developing concentration further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision.
an4.41:1.5: There is a way of developing concentration further that leads to awareness and comprehension.
an4.41:1.6: There is a way of developing concentration further that leads to the destruction of defilements.
an4.41:2.1: And what is the way of developing concentration further that leads to pleasant abiding here and now?
an4.41:2.2: It’s when a bhikkhu, fully withdrawn from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and dwells in the first stage of meditation … second stage of meditation … third stage of meditation … fourth stage of meditation.
an4.41:2.3: This is the way of developing concentration further that leads to pleasant abiding here and now.
an4.41:3.1: And what is the way of developing concentration further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision?
an4.41:3.2: It’s when a bhikkhu applies his mind to the perception of light, focusing on the perception of day:
an4.41:3.3: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.
an4.41:3.4: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.
an4.41:3.5: This is the way of developing concentration further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision.
an4.41:4.1: And what is the way of developing concentration further that leads to awareness and comprehension?
an4.41:4.2: It’s when a bhikkhu knows feelings as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.
an4.41:4.3: They know perceptions as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away. They know thoughts as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.
an4.41:4.4: This is the way of developing concentration further that leads to awareness and comprehension.
an4.41:5.1: And what is the way of developing concentration further that leads to the destruction of defilements?
an4.41:5.2: It’s when a bhikkhu meditates observing the arising and passing away in the five grasping aggregates.
an4.41:5.3: ‘This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the passing away of form.
an4.41:5.4: This is feeling, this is the arising of feeling, this is the passing away of feeling.
an4.41:5.5: This is perception, this is the arising of perception, this is the passing away of perception.
an4.41:5.6: This is volition, this is the arising of volition, this is the passing away of volition.
an4.41:5.7: This is consciousness, this is the arising of consciousness, such is the passing away of consciousness.’
an4.41:5.8: This is the way of developing concentration further that leads to the destruction of defilements.
an4.41:5.9: These are the four ways of developing concentration further.
an4.41:5.10: And it was in this connection that I said in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Puṇṇaka’:
an4.41:6.1: ‘Having appraised the world high and low,
an4.41:6.2: there is nothing in the world that disturbs them.
an4.41:6.3: Peaceful, unclouded, untroubled, <j>with no need for hope,
an4.41:6.4: they’ve crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare.’”
